# Reciprocal CM density: an exact terminal cancellation and the remaining scalar contract Status: LOCAL PARTIAL / RESULT_ONLY COMPOSE / NOT INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED / NOT SOURCE PUBLISHED. This is one faithful recovery appendix, not a new paper, Tool, numerical experiment, Native result, or proof that the old scalar comparison vanishes. The independent original scalar kappa is still not defined by the recovered input contracts. It is never defined here from a target discrepancy. Author of this recovery and its explicit composition: EM-PUBLIC-7CDA51, the same warm actor, SID MCP-9030ae3a22074e3dbc31679b7090f6b0. The preceding activity publication is genuinely closed at Source 6b23363bd6e6486d58be5da158e3411550b381ff, checkpoint 54 / 225 readbacks. This descriptive fact supplies no mathematical authority. Goal OPEN; all original STOP, UNKNOWN, budget and qualification boundaries remain. Root supplied routing and custody control, not mathematical construction or a vote. ## 1. The recovered question and the precise result The 10599-byte local directed-collaboration note `COMMON_DENSITY_FIXED_C_GREEN_AND_LITERAL_RESIDUAL.md` ends with the unproved comparison Phi(D0) - F_CM/(9 g^2) = kappa + T_m + 2 W_m/g. (R1) It is not the missing Student coefficient/contour caller. Its own local status, rather than its title or old check counts, governs its qualification. All quantities on the left of (R1), and T_m and W_m on its right, now have the explicit finite constructors below. Their recovered definitions and elementary identities give the equivalent comparison Phi((y-1)/(1-x)) - OLD-R - 6 tau = kappa. (R2) The quotient in (R2) is a polynomial of degree at most 3m-1. This is an exact equivalence, including every original reciprocal range and boundary factor. It is not an evaluation of either side, a proof of (R1), or a new constructor for kappa. For any independently specified scalar kappa in F_p the two equations have the same truth value. To turn this into an instantiated comparison with the original target, the original independent definition and normalization of that scalar are still needed. The new useful preservation here is the explicit cancellation of the unweighted T_m terminal polynomial against the rho^m terminal in D0. The underlying Gauss connection, reciprocal reflection, fixed-C dictionary, Wilson normalization and finite summation by parts are old mechanisms, rederived below for this consumer and credited as such. The two specifically inspected old target/prefix notes do not literally display (R2); this bounded textual observation is not a claim of general novelty or absence elsewhere. ## 2. Literal finite carrier and legal moment domain Let p=6m+1 be prime, p congruent to 13 or 19 modulo 24, and N=3m. Work in F_p throughout; m>=2. Every integer range below remains an integer range. Reducing a coefficient such as N=-1/2 in F_p never extends a terminating sum. Set g = binom(3m,m), a_i = (1/6)_i (1/3)_i / ((1/2)_i i!), 0<=i<=m, A(z) = sum_(i=0)^m a_i z^i, rho(x) = x(4x-3)^2, y(x) = g A(rho(x)). (R3) All factors divided by in these a_i are units. The recovered original normalization calls g the unit h_0=h_N, with total coefficient sum 1. Here the actual scalar g and the actual polynomial used by the comparison are the explicit ones in (R3); the proof does not replace them with a scalar fitted to a residual. Nor does it use an additional assertion about an unspecified Heun polynomial. The old p-adic memo's divisible scalar also called g is a different object and is not used. The original CM0 conditions A(1/2)=V(1/2)=0 are retained as conditional model premises. They are not proved unconditionally here. Define the original connected Gauss polynomial V(w) = sum_(i=0)^m (1/6)_i (1/3)_i w^i/(i!)^2. The finite identities needed here are A(1)=1/g, V(w)=g A(1-w), y(1)=1, V'(1/2)=-g A'(1/2). (R4) For completeness, in F_p the three parameters 1/6, 1/3, 1/2 equal -m, -2m, -3m. The terminating Vandermonde identity gives A(1)=(1/6)_m/(1/2)_m=m!(2m)!/(3m)!=1/g. The same finite identity applied after j derivatives at 1 gives the coefficient of w^j in g A(1-w). Its remaining factor is g (-1)^j (1/6)_(m-j)/(1/2)_m = 1/j!, 0<=j<=m, because (1/6)_m/(1/6)_(m-j)=(-1)^j j!. This proves the connection in (R4), not merely its endpoint value. These are finite polynomial identities, with no continuation or infinite-series hypothesis. In particular y(1)=1 and both quotients below are genuine polynomials. One can also identify the differential carrier directly: A is annihilated by D_A=z(1-z) d_z^2+(1/2-3z/2) d_z-1/18. Its coefficient recurrence follows from the ratio of a_(i+1) to a_i; its top factor m+1/6 is zero in F_p. The chain rule gives, for every polynomial B, H[B(rho(x))] = -18(4x-1) (D_A B)(rho(x)), H=2x(x-1)(4x-1)d_x^2+(20x^2-15x+1)d_x+(4x-1). Thus the explicit y in (R3) solves the original homogeneous polynomial carrier. This verification does not establish CM0 or any scalar comparison. For f(x)=sum f_l x^l of degree at most N-1 define the actual six moment functionals I_c(f)=sum_l f_l c^(l+1)/(l+1), J_c(f)=sum_l f_l c^(l+1)/(2l+1), Phi(f)=2 I_(1/2)(f)+8 J_(1/2)(f) -I_1(f)/3+8 J_1(f)/3 -7 I_(1/4)(f)/3+20 J_(1/4)(f)/3. (R5) In particular J_c uses c^(l+1), not c^(2l+1). The largest I divisor is N

The full OLD-R cutoff and F_CM identity Define independently, for 1<=i<=m, Htri_i=sum_(r=1)^i [1+6(i-r)]D_r, W_i=t_i Htri_i, W_0=0, OLD-R=2 sum_(i=1)^m a_i W_i, M_R=sum_(i=1)^m S_(i-1)(W_i-W_(i-1)), q_r=(t_m/g)[1+6(m-r)] -sum_(i=r)^m a_i t_i[1+6(i-r)], 1<=r<=m. (R15) Finite summation by parts, using S_(m-1)=1/g-a_m and W_0=0, proves M_R=W_m/g-OLD-R/2=sum_(r=1)^m D_r q_r. The second equality is the finite interchange of the defining W triangles. At r=m the source is q_m=t_m(1/g-a_m); at r=1 its entire low-index contribution is retained. Thus (R10) also gives M_R=eta_N sum_(r=1)^m e_(N-r)q_r/(r t_r). (R16) Use the actual independently prescribed low/high source, not a target-defined replacement: F_CM=sum_(r=1)^m e_(N-r) [q_r/(r t_r)-6 V'_* E_(r-1)^adj(1/2)] -6 V'_* sum_(r=m+1)^N e_(N-r) E_(r-1)^adj(1/2). (R17) All r t_r divisors in (R17) are units. Applying (R14) and (R16), with their unchanged ranges, gives eta_N F_CM=M_R+(3/4)C_*V'_*=M_R-3 tau. (R18) This is the recovered old reciprocal source identity. The last sum in (R17) cannot be dropped merely because OLD-R itself ends at m. Equations (R12) and (R18) give the actual normalization F_CM/(9g^2)=-2 M_R+6 tau. (R19) ## 5. Terminal cancellation and the exact remaining obligation The recovered prescribed T triangle is f_k(x)=(1-4x)^2 rho(x)^k, 0<=k
